# Tomato sauce

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the tomato sauce came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-tomato-sauce" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-tomato-sauce-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of tomato sauce, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach tomato sauce

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach tomato sauce comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Tomato sauce, as sold from metal can, all retail samples had tin higher at 181 µg/kg, against 56 µg/kg for cellulosic carton, all retail samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Muniz LP, Santos LMG, Couto KLM, Jacob SC · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Evaluation of metals in tomato sauces stored in different types of packaging</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Muniz LP, Santos LMG, Couto KLM, Jacob SC · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Evaluation of metals in tomato sauces stored in different types of packaging</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

## Tomato sauce FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-tomato-sauce" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-tomato-sauce" data-question="What heavy metals are found in tomato sauce?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in tomato sauce?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Fe and As in tomato sauce, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-tomato-sauce" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-tomato-sauce" data-question="How do heavy metals get into tomato sauce?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into tomato sauce?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, tomato sauce from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than tomato sauce from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Muniz LP, Santos LMG, Couto KLM, Jacob SC · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Evaluation of metals in tomato sauces stored in different types of packaging</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Tomato sauce, as sold from cellulosic carton, all retail samples had lead higher at 57 µg/kg, against 35 µg/kg for metal can, all retail samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Muniz LP, Santos LMG, Couto KLM, Jacob SC · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Evaluation of metals in tomato sauces stored in different types of packaging</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/muniz2018-tomato-sauce-packaging-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-tomato-sauce" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-tomato-sauce" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in tomato sauce?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in tomato sauce?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, tomato sauce, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (2.65 µg/kg) and the highest in EMRO (350 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in WPRO (18.2 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (20 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
